descripcion: At C1 the issue is not knowing phrasal verbs — it is that you avoid them and reach for the Latinate synonym, which is transparent to a Spanish speaker and therefore comfortable. The result is technically correct English that sounds like a translation: *investigate* instead of *look into*, *tolerate* instead of *put up with*, *postpone* instead of *put off*. This week the Latinate options are banned.

filas: *turn off the light* / *turn the light off*
*put up with*, *come up with*, *look forward to*

ejemplos.texto: *I got into it through a friend and ended up sinking about ten years into it.*
*I've been meaning to take it back up, but I keep putting it off.*
*It started as something to wind down with and turned into a second job.*
*I can't put up with the online side of it any more.*
*I lose track of time completely when I'm tinkering with it.*

notas: Register is not uniformly informal: *carry out*, *point out* and *bring about* are fully acceptable in formal writing.
Many phrasal verbs are polysemous. *Pick up* has at least six senses; learn them by context, not by list.
Three-part verbs are the ones learners most often mangle, because the middle particle looks droppable and is not.

contraste.es: Spanish has no phrasal verbs, so a Spanish speaker's default retrieval is always the Latinate verb — which exists in English but sits one register higher. That mismatch, not error, is what makes advanced English sound stiff.
contraste.de: German separable verbs make phrasal verbs feel natural (nachgehen – look into), so German speakers produce them readily. The trap is similar-looking particles with different meanings (auskommen means get by, not come out).
contraste.it: Italian has its own verbi sintagmatici (andare avanti – go on, tirare fuori – bring out), so verb + particle is a familiar idea. Italian speakers can build on these to use English phrasal verbs more actively.
contraste.fr: French has no phrasal verbs, so the default is the Latinate verb (examiner – examine), which sits one register higher than look into. That mismatch is what makes advanced English sound stiff.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has no phrasal verbs, so the default is the Latinate verb (investigar – investigate), which sits one register higher than look into. That mismatch is what makes advanced English sound stiff.

errores: *Discuss about* — no preposition. Contrast with *talk about*.
Pronoun after the particle: *turn on it*.
Defaulting to the Latinate verb, which is the whole point this week.

redemittel.expresion: to take up / take back up

traducciones.de: sich etwas ausdenken / auf etwas kommen

autochequeo: Twelve different phrasal verbs — count them.
Any pronoun sitting after a particle?
Did I split a three-part verb?
Did any Latinate verb slip through?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on phrasal verbs. (1) List each one and check the particle and the separation. (2) Flag every Latinate verb where a phrasal one would sound more natural, and give it. (3) Flag any register mismatch. (4) Check pronoun placement. Do not rewrite the text.

es: *sacar adelante* rendered as *take forward* instead of *pull through* or *see through*.
de: *durchziehen* rendered as *pull through*, which means 'survive', instead of *see through* or *push through*.
it: *portare avanti* rendered as *bring forward*, which means 'move earlier', instead of *carry on with* or *press ahead with*.
fr: *mener à bien* rendered as *lead to well* instead of *see through* or *carry out*.
pt: *levar adiante* rendered as *carry ahead* instead of *carry on with* or *press ahead with*.
